note: Seed measures from the Philadelphia study (GEOG 376, 2025). Per-vintage sources are mandatory: table definitions drift between decennial-anchored redesigns.

measures.label: Aggregate gross rent
measures.universe: Renter-occupied housing units paying cash rent (both vintages, per the table shells).

legacy_derives.note: The Philadelphia study's definition (GEOG 376, 2025): B25065 divided by all renter-occupied units (B25003_003), which includes no-cash-rent units outside B25065's universe. Biased low wherever no-cash-rent units are common. Kept only so the Phase 04 replication can reproduce the study and measure the difference; not for new indices.

measures.label: Aggregate home value

top_bin.note: Top published bin is "$1,000,000 or more" (025). Registry v2 said collapse_from 024, which would have valued the $750,000-$999,999 bin at $1.25M; corrected in v3 from the label text.

Publishes three bins at or above $1M (025 $1,000,000-$1,499,999, 026 $1,500,000-$1,999,999, 027 $2,000,000 or more). All three are collapsed to the same $1.25M so both vintages treat homes worth $1M+ identically. This understates tracts with many $1.5M+ homes.

measures.bin_rule: Collapse point is set from label text, not by cell number: every bin whose lower bound is at least $1,000,000 (the lower bound of 2006-2010's open-ended top bin) gets the top midpoint. Other bins use (lower + upper + 1) / 2; 'Less than $10,000' is 0-9,999, midpoint 5,000. The build re-parses the vintage's labels and fails if they disagree with the bins recorded here.
measures.top_midpoint_provenance: The $1,250,000 top-bin midpoint comes from the source Philadelphia study (GEOG 376, JMU, 2025), not from Census. Census publishes no midpoint for an open-ended bin; this is a modeling choice, not a derived value.
measures.top_midpoint_alternative: Revisit later: Pareto interpolation (fit a Pareto tail to the upper bins and take the open bin's mean) is the rigorous alternative, as used for Census medians in open-ended intervals.
measures.caution: Bin structure differs between vintages. The top midpoint is an assumption, not a measurement.

measures.label: Bachelor's degree or higher, age 25+

summary_file_substitute.note: B15003 does not exist in 2006-2010. Recomputed from B15002 (sex by educational attainment, population 25+): male bachelor's, master's, professional and doctorate (015-018) plus the same four for women (032-035), over 001. Labels checked against the 2010 lookup file. Same RSS + proportion MOE method as 2016-2020.

Subject tables are not in the Summary File. Recomputed from B15003 (bachelor's + master's + professional + doctorate over population 25+), the definition S1501_C02_015 publishes. Estimates should agree with S1501. The numerator MOE is the root-sum-square of the component MOEs and the percent MOE uses the proportion formula, the Census-documented method for derived estimates (ACS Handbook, 'Calculating Measures of Error for Derived Estimates'). Census computes S1501's published MOE directly, so the two MOEs can differ slightly.

measures.caution: Subject table. Separate Summary File and separate API endpoint from detailed tables.

measures.label: Non-Hispanic white share of population
measures.caution: Near-zero baselines produce percent changes in the hundreds or thousands that mean nothing. This is the reason the index standardizes rather than ranking raw percent change.

cash_rent_renter_households.note: 'With cash rent:' in both 2006-2010 and 2016-2020. This is B25065's universe. B25070_001 was rejected: its total includes a 'Not computed' line (no cash rent or zero income).

2006-2010.note: B15002 'Total:' is population 25 years and over, the same universe as S1501_C01_006.

2016-2020.note: Same universe (population 25 years and over) as S1501_C01_006.

bachelors_plus.note: Numerator of pct_bachelors_plus, kept as a count (v5) so the harmonizer can apportion it and recompute the percent; a percent cannot be apportioned.

nh_white.note: Numerator of pct_nh_white (Not Hispanic or Latino: White alone), kept as a count (v5) for the same reason.

race_universe.note: B03002 total: the denominator pct_nh_white is computed over (v6). Equals B01003 in Virginia's tracts, but not guaranteed everywhere.

jam_note: jam_values are missing data and become null. controlled_moe_value appears only in MOE fields: the estimate is controlled to an independent total, has no sampling error, and becomes an MOE of 0. In an estimate field it is an error.
